messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
No product name was given, so I've used a placeholder (`Rev`) — swap it for yours.

---

# Pricing

Rev reads your diffs and leaves comments a senior engineer would leave. Start free, upgrade when the review queue starts hurting.

## Solo — $0

For one person and public repos.

You get unlimited reviews on open-source projects, plus three private repos. Rev comments on pull requests, flags the obvious things (null derefs, unhandled promises, a test that asserts nothing), and stays quiet otherwise. No credit card. No trial clock.

Where it stops: no custom rules, no team settings, community support only.

## Team — $18 per developer / month

For teams of 3 to 40 who are tired of the "LGTM" rubber stamp.

Everything in Solo, on unlimited private repos. Write your own review rules in plain English — "we never call the payments client from a request handler" — and Rev enforces them on every PR. It learns from what your reviewers approve and reject, so it stops repeating suggestions your team has already waved off twice.

Also: GitHub and GitLab, Slack alerts, a monthly digest of what keeps getting flagged. Email support, one business day.

## Enterprise — talk to us

For regulated shops and anyone over 200 engineers.

Self-hosted or single-tenant cloud. SSO with SCIM provisioning, audit logs, SOC 2 report on request, and a contract that says your code never trains a model. You get a named engineer who knows your stack and answers in a shared channel.

Annual billing. Custom seat pricing above 500 developers.

---

Every plan: cancel anytime, and your review history exports as JSON.
